source_observations.locator: Kāśikā 5.1.59, source record 51059; Nyāsa and Bālamanoramā
source_observations.observation: Ten separate received lexical treatments. Conventional row senses and inherent grammatical number are retained.
Five offerings and five-footed metre in one paragraph, with nominative paṅktiḥ, instrumental compound and simple genitive.
Twenty through seventy appear as six instrumental singulars. The horses are separately instrumental plural.
Eighty, ninety and one hundred continue the same construction. The hundred is neuter.

source_observations.locator: van Nooten and Holland, metrically restored Ṛgveda 2.18.4–6, UT Austin
source_observations.observation: The editorial syllabification of sixty in verse 5 differs from the received Pada form; the earlier small numbers show a different declensional class.
A dative singular of a hundred in the offered-price frame.
Class of five or ten, ḍati or kan. The i in the stipulated ḍati treatment here is explanatory.
Ḍaṇ for named Brāhmaṇa texts. The locative specifies what is named. Ṭi loss is attributed to the ḍ marker.
